The Helan Mountains, sometimes called a "mountain island in the sky," form a barrier between the semi-arid Ordos Plateau and the Yellow River Valley on one side and the arid deserts of the Alxa Plateau to the west on the other. Like the rugged ranges of western North America's Great Basin, the Helan Range isolates dense conifer forests and may support unique, endemic communities of plants and animals. The ecoregion has received little scientific attention, yet it holds several rare species, among them blue sheep, blue-eared pheasants, and the endemic Helan pika. Commercial logging remains a serious threat, and the habitat destruction it causes endangers the region's high biological diversity.

A New Frontier in Wikitravel Data Representation

Some of our data representations will be unique to Wikitravel, setting us apart from other organizations. The big change, though, is the Turtle RDF standard.

Turtle lets us create custom RDF schemas directly. That means we can use the same wiki techniques we already know to develop our own schemas, without needing a separate platform.

We can even build a schema on our shared Wikitravel site, at Shared:Wikitravel:Schema. Once created, elements within this schema will be accessible with the namespace wts: (Wikitravel schema) in Turtle.

This is the future of structured, scalable wiki data. #Wikitravel #RDF #DataScience #Technology

# Conservation of Nose-Touch Avoidance Across *C. elegans* and Relatives

Nose touch avoidance behavior is conserved in five of the six species tested (Figure 5A). In *C. tripartitum*, animals showed an overall avoidance rate below 10% after the first few positive trials, suggesting this species adapts to the nose-touch stimulus faster than *C. elegans* and the others (Figure 5A). During the first three trials, however, *C. tripartitum* responded at levels quantitatively similar to *C. elegans* (Figure S2 in Additional file 2).

Ablating the ASH neurons in five nose-touch responsive species eliminated nose-touch avoidance (Figure 5A). Four of the five species still responded to nose touch in 20–30% of trials (Figure 5A), but *Caenorhabditis* sp. 3 was different. Its ASH-ablated animals completely lost the ability to respond to nose touch (Figure 5A).

Ablation of the AWC neuron, by contrast, had no effect on the response to nose touch in any of the species (Figure S3 in Additional file 2).

UPO-06: PrhI Gene Synthesis
UPO-06 carries the coding sequence for prhI from *Ralstonia solanacearum*, an ECF sigma factor needed for transcription driven by the Prh signal transduction system. PrhR activates the gene, which then directs sigma factor expression through activation of the PprhJ promoter. The sequence has been optimized for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

UPO-11: PprhJ Promoter Synthesis
UPO-11 contains the PprhJ promoter region, which responds to plant cell contact through signal transduction mediated by PrhA and PrhR, and is activated by the ECF sigma factor PrhI. The sequence has been optimized for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

Subject: Key Findings on foxl2 Expression Patterns in Trout

Dear Customer,

Here is a summary of our findings on foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both foxl2 transcripts were expressed very early in development (Figure 2). foxl2a expression was highly restricted in the male, while the diverged paralog foxl2b was present in most adult extragonadal tissues examined (see Additional file 2).

In contrast, foxl2b expression was highly restricted in adult female tissues, essentially confined to the skin, gill, and ovary. foxl2b expression in the testis was very strong, which fits well with previous findings showing foxl2b presence alongside the absence of foxl2a in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

Taken together, these results suggest that foxl2b may act as a critical regulator of male-specific genes (such as cyp19b1), particularly later in development.

Thank you for your interest in our research.

Best regards,

[Your Name]

Additionality examines the counterfactual: what would have happened under the status quo had the REC not been purchased or contracted. While many additionality testing frameworks exist, the core question stays the same: did the project's financial survival depend on REC revenues? Without verified proof of additionality, RECs cannot be treated as genuine emissions offsets.

Starting from the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975), we derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation and, from it, the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Using only the linear dispersion relation for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), known as the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). The leading-order solution shows that the modified curvature terms of the MMSE have significant effects, while the slope square terms stay negligible, consistent with the mild-slope assumption. We therefore kept all the modified curvature terms that the MSE neglects, which produced a uniform model.

We built a numerical model with the finite element method (FEM) to predict wave scattering by a varying bottom. In general, the uniform model captures the main features of waves over different sea beds, including sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. For sinusoidal beds, the uniform model agrees more closely with experimental data than other established models. For man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model agree more closely with experimental data than the results of Kirby (1986).

A key result of the FEM model is its application to wave transformation over arbitrarily-varying bathymetry.

The myth in the Phaedrus is more intense than anything that came before it, though it deals with a different subject. Instead of a future life, it describes a former one, showing a deep conflict between reason, supported by passion or righteous indignation, and the animal instincts within us. In that earlier life, the human soul traveled in the company of some god and saw truth in the form of the universal before birth, and our present existence is the outcome of a struggle that took place then. This world is a relative construct, often projected into a future, much as we wonder where men were before their birth or what awaits them after death. The question "Where were men before birth?" feels unfamiliar and unnatural to us, yet it carries as much force and reach as the other. In the Phaedrus, the "spiritual combat" of this life is only a figure of speech. The majesty and power of the whole passage, especially the proem beginning "The mind through all her being is immortal," cannot really be captured in another language.

Subject: A Note on Buraq

Dear Friend,

The world once existed as a blend of reality and myth, and the distinction between the two only became clear with modern comparative biology. Even so, science has not erased the in-between zone where a figure like Buraq lives. We need such transitional objects to connect two things that seem far apart: empirical knowledge and spiritual experience.

Her presence in contemporary culture works as a bridge between rationalist taxonomies and the leftover power of myth. The idea shows up most forcefully in the Islamic transport industry, where Buraq, a figure combining piety and speed, recurs as a patron saint. She gives her name to airlines from Libya to Indonesia, bus companies, freight ships, motorcycle taxis, a space camp, an engineering college, and even Pakistan's first drone.

Because Buraq is fluid as an aesthetic and linguistic object, she adapts easily to commercial use: she presides over wings and wheels, but she is also used to sell plastic and PVC, heavy metal, and heavy-duty diesel (BURAQ LUBRICANTS), Indian food, and surgical instruments.

MapleStory Monsters: A Survival Guide to the Underworld

Welcome to MapleStory. There are thousands of monsters roaming the world, so here is a quick breakdown of where they live and how to survive.

The weak monsters are the most common foes, and they are found by towns. They wander aimlessly, even if you bump into them, so don't worry. Just take the damage they deal.

The dangerous ones live deep in dungeons.

The aggro mechanic matters. Monsters usually roam aimlessly, even if you bump into them. But if you attack an enemy or cast a debuff on it, you aggro it. That means you get its attention, and it will try to attack you back.

Most enemies attack by trying to run into you over and over again.

Against these persistent attackers, the easiest thing to do is attack them repeatedly. Your attacks usually have enough knockback to keep them in place.

Sometimes you will need to jump over them to dodge their attacks entirely.

For the complete list of monsters, check out the MapleStory/Monsters/Complete list.

Aggro is a two-way street. Stay safe and keep attacking.

The region came from Gondwana. During the Cretaceous period, the Deccan Plate broke away from Gondwanaland, drifted north, and later rejoined the northern Eurasian continent. Geological uplift then formed the Western Ghats Mountains, which caught the southwestern monsoon rains and produced a moisture gradient: wet on the windward side, drier habitats toward the leeward side. We want to share some important information about early hearing development. Human beings typically develop spoken language within the first few years of life. Hearing impairment can prevent the ability to speak and also hinder the ability to understand spoken language.

By the time it becomes apparent that a severely hearing-impaired (deaf) child has a hearing deficit, communication problems may have already caused issues within the family and hindered social skills. If the child is part of a Deaf community where sign language is used instead of spoken language, these challenges can be mitigated (please see our article on Deaf Culture).

In many developed countries, evaluations for hearing occur during the newborn period to prevent the inadvertent isolation of a deaf child within a hearing family. Sign language is a full means of communication, but literacy ultimately depends on the ability to understand speech. In most written language, the sound of the word is coded in symbols.

A person who hears well enough to learn to speak and read will retain the ability to read even if their hearing becomes too impaired to hear voices. A person who never heard well enough to learn to speak is rarely able to read proficiently (see [4]). Most evidence suggests that early identification of hearing impairment is key to ensuring a child with very insensitive hearing learns spoken language effectively. Listening also plays an important role in learning a second language.

We hope this information helps you understand the importance of early intervention. If you have any further questions, please reach out.

Warm regards,

Transduction is the conversion of physical and chemical signals into neural impulses. In the nervous system, it is the basic process of translating stimuli into electrical signals. In sensory transduction, physical or chemical inputs are changed by specialized sensory receptors into electrical impulses that travel to the brain.

The visual system is a good example. In the retina, rod and cone cells link the physical environment to neural communication. When light strikes these photoreceptors, it causes a conformational change in the protein rhodopsin. This molecular shift starts a cascade of events that alters the electrochemical gradient of the photoreceptor. The reduction in this gradient causes a decrease in the electrical signals sent to the brain. So more light hitting the photoreceptor results in fewer electrical impulses, and the brain uses this to decode the visual world with precision.

Mobile Gaming: The Next Evolution of Co-Creation

Mobile internet is expanding the immersive potential of storytelling through electronic games that run on portable, location-aware interfaces. This is the latest step in a decades-long evolution of electronic games that aim to make the player more than an avatar in a gameworld, turning them into a co-author alongside the original designers.

Location-aware interfaces let players pull places from the physical world into their gameworld, and the reverse, something no earlier interactive media could do. Beyond giving players a role in worldmaking, mobile games abandon linear narratives in favor of cooperative storytelling built on the player's experience of place.

The "author-player" worldmaking idea is not new, but mobile games push the process past the limits of traditional video games. By extending worldmaking beyond the screen and into the physical world, location-aware interfaces use the player's sensory experiences of real places as storytelling tools.

In our essay, we theorize the unique storytelling potential of mobile games and describe our experience trying to put that potential into practice through the design and implementation of our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.

Subject: Study Results: Lung Tissue Volume and Aeration Analysis

Dear Customer,

I hope this message finds you well.

Below are the key findings from our analysis of lung tissue volume and functional changes.

The total volume of lung tissue was calculated using the formula: volume of lung tissue = number of voxels × volume of the voxel, provided the compartment considered has a CT number above zero.

The change in functional residual capacity resulting from PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) was computed as the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between PEEP and ZEEP states. Alveolar derecruitment was defined as the difference in gas volume within poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions between these same conditions.

We also computed the changes in gas volume from PEEP withdrawal specifically in normally aerated lung regions, characterized by CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).

As previously described in reference [21], the distribution of lost lung aeration for each patient (lung morphology) was classified as diffuse, patchy, and lobar based on the distribution of CT attenuations at ZEEP.

Subject: Tips for Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), often simply called the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is made up of many former industrial cities, including Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

The region has around five million inhabitants, which makes it considerably larger than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. There are plenty of motorways here, but hitchhiking can be hard because of the complicated network of minor roads. The main motorways are the A1, A2, and A3.

If you plan to hitch here, stay on these primary motorways. The smaller roads are very difficult to use because there is very little transit traffic. Germany is generally a pleasant country for hitchhiking, but the Ruhr Area is by far the most unpleasant part of it from this point of view. Hitching inside the Ruhr Area is comparable to hitching in a big city like Istanbul; the cities are independent, but for travelers they all feel like districts of one huge city.

We hope this information helps you plan your trip safely and enjoyably.

Best regards,

[Your Name/Company]
